structure:
repos/trade-imports-reference-data is a small Java / Spring Boot service (about 1,650 lines of main code in scope, about 2,100 lines of unit and integration tests, about 1,000 lines of MDM JSON fixtures). It fronts MDM (the Defra master data service) and serves reference lists to the frontends through three REST endpoints: GET /countries (CountriesController, with an optional blocks filter and subdivisions), GET /ports-of-entry (PortsOfEntryController, with port types and list order), and GET /commodities plus POST /commodities/species-check (CommoditiesController, CommoditySearchService, SpeciesCheckService). Everything comes from MDM through MdmClient (Feign: /mdm/geo/countries, /mdm/trade/bcp/poes, /mdm/trade/product/search, /mdm/trade/product/commodities, /mdm/trade/product/commodities/{code}/species) and MdmService, with countries and ports cached (CacheConfig) and MDM failures mapped to HTTP errors by GlobalExceptionHandler and MdmErrorDecoder. Its rulings are the ADRs under doc/adr/ (0002: reference-data serves several domains until they get too large); there is no decisions ledger. Of the scope's seven lists, countries, ports, and commodities with species and commodity identifiers (commodity codes) are served today; transporters, document types and certification purposes have no endpoint, model or MDM call anywhere in the repo, so they are gaps. Left out as outside scope: metrics, observability, logging, tracing, TLS trust store, proxy, Mongo, AWS and auth-token plumbing (src/main/java/.../metrics, logging, filter, interceptor, configuration/tls and the non-MDM configuration classes) and CI workflows, except where they change what a caller receives. Cut into 3 parts by reference list: countries and ports; commodities and species; the service's shared contract (docs, ADRs, error handling, MDM configuration) together with the scope's missing lists.

Extracted in 3 parts:
Part 1, Countries and ports of entry: Part 1, countries and ports of entry. Read in full: CountriesController, Country, SubDivision (countries package); PortsOfEntryController, PortOfEntry, PortType, PortListOrder (portsofentry package); MdmService and MdmClient (claimed only for getCountries, getPortsOfEntry, the /mdm/geo/countries and /mdm/trade/bcp/poes calls and the shared body and trace-id handling those two use); the MDM models MdmCountry, MdmSubDivision, MdmBlock, MdmCodedValue, MdmPortOfEntry, MdmPortsResponse; CacheConfig; the unit tests CountriesControllerTest, CountryTest, PortsOfEntryControllerTest, PortOfEntryTest, PortTypeTest and the countries and ports tests of MdmServiceTest; the integration tests CountriesControllerIT, CountriesControllerCacheExpiryIT, PortsOfEntryControllerIT; and the MDM fixtures mdm-countries-response.json and mdm-poe-response.json. Covered: GET /countries (optional blocks parameter, code, name and subDivisions fields, GB removed, block filtering, A to Z by name, empty list when MDM has none), GET /ports-of-entry (no parameters, code, name and type fields, the three port types from MDM traffic, airports then seaports then rail then unknown, each A to Z ignoring case and spacing, then by code), the MDM_COUNTRIES_CACHE and MDM_POE_CACHE caches (60-minute default expiry, 20 entries, empty results not cached, countries cached per blocks value), the two MDM calls with the GBNAG system and subscription-key header, the MDM-unavailable failures for a missing body or result, and every test in the nine test files that proves countries or ports behaviour. Gaps recorded for what the slice is silent on: a single country or port by code, filtering ports by type or by what a port is designated for, and subdivision order.
Part 2, Commodities, species and commodity codes: Part 2, commodities and species. Read in full: the commodities package (CommoditiesController, CommoditySearchService, SpeciesCheckService and the five records CommoditySearchResponse, CommodityGroup, CommodityLine, CommoditySpecies, SpeciesCheckRequest, SpeciesCheckResponse), the MDM client layer (MdmService and MdmClient in full, claiming only searchProducts, getCommodities and getCommoditySpecies; the records MdmCommodity, MdmSpecies, MdmProductPage, MdmProductSearchResult), the five commodity unit test files (CommoditiesControllerTest, CommoditySearchServiceTest, SpeciesCheckServiceTest, CommoditySpeciesTest, CommodityGroupTest), CommoditiesControllerIT, the product, commodity and species tests of MdmServiceTest, and the six MDM fixtures (commodities, search 0102, species of 0102, search cattle, bison, dog). Covered: GET /commodities (q, page, size, the two-character minimum, how MDM species and commodity rows become species matches, the germinal exclusion, de-duplication by code and Latin name, grouping by code in MDM order, the page-size cap and what total counts), POST /commodities/species-check (request and response fields, validation, per-code paged lookups, exact-case matching, every answer), the three MDM product calls with their dataset and paging, how MDM failures surface on these endpoints, the OpenAPI descriptions, what the fixtures show of MDM's commodity and species data, and every test that proves this behaviour. Gaps recorded: no commodity description in the response, no germinal search, no commodity hierarchy browsing, and no caching of product calls.
Part 3, Service contract, rulings and missing lists: Part 3 of 3, the service's shared contract and the scope's missing lists. Read in full: README.md (purpose, endpoints, port, ports-of-entry ordering, commodity search notes, metrics and configuration notes), AGENTS.md (code-quality notes for agents, no behaviour), the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-reference-data.md (purpose, owns / does not own, integrations, MDM commodity search behaviour, stack, how to run), ADR 0001 (record decisions as ADRs) and ADR 0002 (one shared reference-data service for several domains until one grows too large), application.yml and application-local.yml, MdmConfiguration, MdmErrorDecoder, GlobalExceptionHandler, the five exception classes, GlobalExceptionHandlerTest, MdmErrorDecoderTest and TokenEndpointUnavailableIT. To say which exceptions a caller can actually meet, MdmService and MdmClientInterceptor were grepped for where each exception is thrown (MDM no body / no result / no content / no total, MDM unreachable, token endpoint 502-504 or unreachable); NotFoundException and ConflictException are never thrown in src/main. Endpoints were confirmed with a grep of every request mapping in src/main/java: GET /countries, GET /ports-of-entry, GET /commodities, POST /commodities/species-check, and the MDM calls. Claims cover: the stated purpose, endpoints, port and callers; ADR 0002 as a ruling and ADR 0001 as the record-keeping rule; every error response GlobalExceptionHandler gives (status, type, title, detail, traceId, field errors) with the tests that prove each; MdmErrorDecoder's 502/503/504 mapping; the MDM and cache settings that change what a caller receives (base URL, cache TTL, timeouts, subscription key, system and dataset); and three gaps (transporters, document types, certification purposes) found by a case-insensitive repo-wide grep of src/main, src/test/java, doc/, README.md and the workspace page for transporter, haulier, carrier, document type, accompanying document, certification and purpose, which found nothing but the word Purpose as a heading. Page sizes for commodity search belong to part 2 and are only mentioned as documented.

claims.statement: The service serves the list of countries at GET /countries.
GET /countries takes one optional query parameter, blocks, and no other parameter.
claims.quote:
public ResponseEntity<List<Country>> getCountries(
      @RequestParam(required = false, value = "blocks") String blocks)

claims.statement: GET /countries answers 200 OK with a JSON array of countries.
Each country in the response has three fields: code, name and subDivisions.
A country's code is MDM's effectiveAlpha2 (the two-letter country code, such as DE).
A country's name is MDM's effectiveAlias (the short common name, such as "United Kingdom"), not MDM's name or long name.
claims.note: The fixture shows the difference: MDM name "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (the)", effectiveAlias "United Kingdom".

claims.statement: The other MDM country fields (longName, name, independent, statusName, system, the system alias and codes, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveLongName and blocks) are not passed on in the response.
claims.note: Inferred: MdmCountry carries these fields and the Country constructor copies only effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlias and subDivisions.

claims.statement: Each subdivision (a territory or region of a country, such as the Canary Islands of Spain) has two fields: code and name.
claims.quote:
private String code;
  private String name;

claims.statement: A subdivision's code is the value of MDM's coded subdivision code (such as ES-CN), and its name is MDM's subdivision name.
A subdivision MDM gives with no code, or with a code that has no value, is left out of the country's subdivisions.
claims.note: mechanism: drops MDM subdivisions that lack a code.

claims.statement: A country MDM gives with no subdivisions, or with none listed, is served with an empty subDivisions list rather than a missing one.
The blocs list MDM gives on each subdivision is not passed on in the response.
claims.note: Inferred: MdmSubDivision carries blocs and the mapping copies only code and name. Subdivisions are not filtered by block either.

claims.statement: The countries list comes back sorted by name, A to Z.
claims.note: The comparison is plain string order, so it is case-sensitive and not locale-aware, unlike the ports order.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom (MDM effectiveAlpha2 GB) is never in the countries list, and its subdivisions, such as Northern Ireland, go with it.
When blocks is given, a country is listed only if MDM gives it a block with that exact name marked includeCountry true.
claims.note: Block names seen in tests: GBNAG_SPS_EX, GBNAG_PHYTO_EX, OMR. The value is matched as one block name, so a comma-separated list of blocks would match nothing locally.

claims.statement: A country MDM gives with no blocks at all is kept in the list whatever blocks value was asked for.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;
claims.note: mechanism: works on MDM's blocks list per country.

claims.statement: When blocks is not given, no block filter is applied: every country MDM returns, except the United Kingdom, is listed.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: When MDM returns no countries, GET /countries answers 200 OK with an empty list.
When MDM answers the countries request with no body, the service treats MDM as unavailable, with the message "MDM returned no body for countries request for <blocks>".
claims.quote:
throw new MdmUnavailableException(
          "MDM returned no body for %s request for %s".formatted(requestName, requestedFor));
claims.note: How MdmUnavailableException reaches the caller as an HTTP status is the shared error handling, part 3.

claims.statement: The service gets countries from MDM with GET /mdm/geo/countries, sending the subscription key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and the system and blocks query parameters.
The countries request to MDM always sends system GBNAG, and passes the caller's blocks value on unchanged (left out when the caller gave none).
The service gets ports of entry from MDM with GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes, sending the subscription key in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and system GBNAG as a query parameter.
MDM's ports answer is an object whose result field holds the list of ports, each with id, code, name and traffic.
MDM's countries answer is a JSON array of countries, each with its codes, names, independence, status, system, subdivisions and blocks; a block has a name, an includeCountry flag and tags.

The service reads an MDM trace id from the x-ms-middleware-request-id response header on the countries and ports calls, logging it when present and warning when absent, and the request still succeeds without it.
claims.quote: log.warn("No MDM trace id returned for {} request for {}", requestName, requestedFor);

claims.statement: When the connection to MDM is dropped or times out on a countries or ports call, the service reports MDM as unavailable, with the message "MDM unavailable".
claims.quote:
} catch (RetryableException ex) {
      throw new MdmUnavailableException("MDM unavailable", ex);
claims.note: The shared helper is proven for product search in MdmServiceTest; no countries or ports test covers it.

claims.statement: The service serves the list of ports of entry at GET /ports-of-entry, which takes no query parameters.
GET /ports-of-entry answers 200 OK with a JSON array of ports.
Each port in the response has three fields: code, name and type.
A port's code and name are MDM's code and name as given, and MDM's port id is not passed on.
claims.note: MDM codes may hold a space, such as "GB ABD" in the fixture.

claims.statement: Port names are served exactly as MDM gives them: the list order only compares names, it never changes them (so "TILBURY" and "Portsmouth  Quay" with a double space come back unchanged).
claims.quote: Names are only compared in this order, never changed.

claims.statement: A port's type is one of three values: airport, seaport or rail, written in lower case.
A port's type comes from MDM's traffic field: "Airport" gives airport, "Port" gives seaport and "Rail" gives rail, ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces.
A port whose MDM traffic is missing or not one of the three known values is still listed, with type null.
The service logs a warning, once per port code and traffic value, when MDM gives a port a traffic value that is not a known port type.
claims.quote: log.warn("MDM port {} has traffic '{}', which is not a known port type; it is listed last with no type",

claims.statement: The ports list comes back as airports first, then seaports, then rail ports, then ports of unknown type.
claims.quote: Airports, then seaports, then rail ports, then ports of unknown type.

claims.statement: Within each port type group, ports run A to Z by name, ignoring letter case and treating non-breaking spaces and runs of spaces as one space.
claims.quote:
Each group runs A to Z by name ignoring letter case and reading non-breaking and doubled spaces as one,
   * then by code.

claims.statement: Ports with the same type and name are ordered by code.
Every port MDM returns for system GBNAG is listed: the service does not filter ports by type or any other property.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any filter between the MDM result and the response.

claims.statement: When MDM answers the ports request with no body, the service treats MDM as unavailable, with the message "MDM returned no body for ports-of-entry request for GBNAG".
claims.quote: .hasMessage("MDM returned no body for ports-of-entry request for GBNAG");

claims.statement: When MDM's ports answer has no result list, the service treats MDM as unavailable, with the message "MDM returned a ports-of-entry body with no result for GBNAG".
claims.quote:
throw new MdmUnavailableException(
          "MDM returned a ports-of-entry body with no result for " + SYSTEM);

claims.statement: Countries from MDM are cached in a cache named MDM_COUNTRIES_CACHE.
Ports of entry from MDM are cached in a cache named MDM_POE_CACHE.
Cached countries and ports expire 60 minutes after they are fetched by default, set by cache.mdm.ttl-minutes.
The countries and ports caches each hold at most 20 entries.
An empty or missing result from MDM is never cached, so the next request asks MDM again.
Countries are cached separately for each blocks value, so a repeated blocks value is served from the cache and a new one asks MDM.
The cache holds MDM's countries after the United Kingdom and block filters, and the A to Z sort and mapping to code, name and subdivisions run on every request.
claims.note: mechanism: inferred from @Cacheable on MdmService.getCountries, which returns the filtered list, while sorting and mapping sit in the controller. A list that filters down to empty is not cached.

claims.statement: Each GET /countries and each GET /ports-of-entry request is counted as a lookup and timed.
claims.note: Metrics are outside the source's scope; recorded only because the endpoints do it.

claims.statement: Proven (CountriesControllerTest): a countries request is counted as one "countries" lookup.
Proven (CountriesControllerTest): countries MDM returns as Sweden, Austria, France come back as Austria, France, Sweden.
Proven (CountriesControllerTest, CountryTest): an MDM country DE / Germany is served with code DE, name Germany and no subdivisions.
Proven (CountriesControllerTest): Spain is served with its Canary Islands subdivision (code ES-CN), and Austria with an empty subdivision list.

Proven (CountriesControllerIT, against a stubbed MDM): GET /countries?blocks=GBNAG_SPS_EX lists France before Germany, leaves out the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland, and carries nested subdivisions such as the Canary Islands.
Proven (CountriesControllerIT): the response writes MDM's effectiveAlpha2 as code and effectiveAlias as name ("code":"DE", "name":"Germany").
Proven (CountriesControllerIT): on an empty cache the first countries request calls MDM once, and a second identical request is served from the cache without calling MDM.
Proven (CountriesControllerIT): when MDM first returns no countries, the next request calls MDM again.
Proven (CountriesControllerCacheExpiryIT): with the cache expiry set to zero, two countries requests both call MDM, so an expired entry is fetched again.
claims.note: Expiry is proven for the countries cache only; no test proves ports cache expiry.

claims.statement: Proven (MdmServiceTest): the countries call sends the subscription key, system GBNAG and the caller's blocks value to MDM, and returns MDM's countries, with or without a trace id header.
Proven (MdmServiceTest): the United Kingdom is filtered out, and Martinique is filtered out when its GBNAG_SPS_EX block has includeCountry false even though another block includes it.
Proven (MdmServiceTest): with no blocks value, countries are kept even when their block says includeCountry false.
Proven (MdmServiceTest): a countries answer with no body is reported as MDM unavailable, naming the blocks value.
claims.quote: .hasMessage("MDM returned no body for countries request for GBNAG_SPS_EX");

claims.statement: Proven (MdmServiceTest): the ports call sends the subscription key and system GBNAG, returns MDM's ports with or without a trace id header, and reports MDM unavailable for a missing body or a missing result.
Proven (PortsOfEntryControllerTest): a ports request answers 200 OK and is counted as one "ports-of-entry" lookup.

Proven (PortOfEntryTest): an MDM port with traffic Airport is served as type airport with its code and name, and a port with unknown traffic (Hovercraft) has no type and is warned about once however often it is mapped.
Proven (PortTypeTest): traffic "Airport", "PORT" and " rail " give airport, seaport and rail, and null or unknown traffic gives no type.

Proven (PortsOfEntryControllerIT, against a stubbed MDM of 14 ports): the list comes back as two airports, nine seaports, one rail port and two of unknown type, each group A to Z ignoring case and doubled spaces, in the order Aberdeen Airport, East Midlands Airport, Aberdeen Harbour, Port of Dover, Port of Sheerness, Port of Sheerness, Port of Tyne, Portsmouth Port, Portsmouth  Quay, Teestort, TILBURY, Folkestone, Alpha Ferry Terminal, Beta Quay.
claims.note: The fixture includes traffic " port " (Port of Tyne, typed seaport), "Ferry" and null (both unknown).

claims.statement: Proven (PortsOfEntryControllerIT): two ports both named Port of Sheerness come back ordered by code, "GB SHS" before "GBSHS".

Proven (PortsOfEntryControllerIT): each port is written as code, name and type, such as {"code":"GB ABD","name":"Aberdeen Harbour","type":"seaport"}, and a port of unknown type is written with "type":null.
Proven (PortsOfEntryControllerIT): on an empty cache the first ports request calls MDM once, a second request is served from the cache, and an empty MDM answer is not cached.
There is no way to look up a single country or a single port by its code: only the whole lists are served.
claims.note: Looked at both controllers: each has one GET mapping on its root path and no path variable.

claims.statement: The ports list cannot be narrowed by port type or by what a port is designated to handle (such as live animals or germinal products): GET /ports-of-entry takes no parameters and MDM is asked only by system.
claims.note: The source scope names ports for the live-animals journey; nothing in the slice says which ports suit which commodity.

claims.statement: The order of a country's subdivisions is not set by the service: they come back in the order MDM gives them.
claims.note: Looked in Country.mapSubDivisions and the controller sort: only countries are sorted. No test fixes a subdivision order.

claims.statement: The service exposes a commodity search at GET /commodities, described as searching species by name or commodity code.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/commodities") ... @Operation(summary = "Search species by name or commodity code"

claims.statement: The commodity endpoints are tagged as serving live-animal commodity codes and species from MDM.
claims.quote: @Tag(name = "Commodities", description = "Live-animal commodity codes and species from MDM")

claims.statement: GET /commodities takes an optional search term in the query parameter q, which may be a species name or a commodity code.
claims.quote: @Parameter(description = "Search term: a species name or a commodity code", example = "dog") @RequestParam(value = "q", required = false) String q

claims.statement: GET /commodities takes a zero-based page number in the query parameter page, defaulting to 0 and refusing anything below 0.
GET /commodities takes the most species to list in the query parameter size, defaulting to 100 and limited to between 1 and 100.
claims.quote: @Parameter(description = "Most species to list, from 1 to 100") @RequestParam(defaultValue = "100") @Min(1) @Max(CommoditySearchService.MAXIMUM_PAGE_SIZE) int size ... static final int MAXIMUM_PAGE_SIZE = 100;

claims.statement: GET /commodities answers 400 when the page or size is not valid, 503 when MDM is unavailable, and 200 with the matching species otherwise.
claims.quote: @ApiResponse(responseCode = "200", description = "The matching species") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "400", description = "The page or size is not valid") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "503", description = "MDM unavailable")

claims.statement: The search term is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is used, and a missing term counts as empty.
A trimmed search term shorter than two characters matches nothing: the search answers 200 with a total of 0, the page and size asked for, and no groups, without asking MDM.
claims.quote: static final int MINIMUM_SEARCH_LENGTH = 2; ... if (trimmedSearchTerm.length() < MINIMUM_SEARCH_LENGTH) { ... return CommoditySearchResponse.builder().total(0).page(page).size(size).groups(List.of()).build(); ... "A term shorter than two characters matches nothing."

claims.statement: A search term of two characters or more is sent to MDM's product search with the page and size the caller gave.

The service does not itself tell a search by commodity code apart from a search by species name: both go to MDM's one product search as the same q term, and MDM's answer decides whether species rows or commodity rows come back.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any code-versus-name branch in CommoditySearchService; the IT shows a q of 0102 returning a commodity row and q of dog, cattle or bison returning species rows.

claims.statement: MDM product search returns two kinds of row, species and commodity; a row of any other result type is read as having no type and contributes nothing to the search.
claims.quote: @JsonFormat(with = JsonFormat.Feature.READ_UNKNOWN_ENUM_VALUES_AS_NULL) ResultType resultType ... @JsonProperty("species") SPECIES, @JsonProperty("commodity") COMMODITY ... return null;
claims.note: mechanism: maps MDM product search rows to a commodity code by result type.

claims.statement: A species row from MDM search becomes one species match under the row's commodityCnCode, with the row's speciesName as the Latin name and its commonName.
claims.quote: if (row.resultType() == SPECIES) { return row.commodityCnCode(); } ... Stream.of(new SpeciesMatch(code, row.latinName(), row.commonName())); ... @JsonProperty("speciesName") String latinName
claims.note: mechanism: turns MDM species search rows into code and species pairs.

claims.statement: A commodity row from MDM search contributes one species match per entry in its scientificNames list, each under the row's code; a commodity row with no scientificNames contributes nothing.
claims.quote: if (row.resultType() == COMMODITY) { return row.code(); } ... if (row.species() == null) { return Stream.empty(); } ... @JsonProperty("scientificNames") List<MdmSpecies> species
claims.note: mechanism: expands an MDM commodity search row into its listed species.

claims.statement: An MDM search row with no commodity code (no commodityCnCode on a species row, no code on a commodity row, or no result type) is left out of the search.
claims.quote: String code = codeOf(row); if (code == null) { return Stream.empty(); }
claims.note: mechanism: drops MDM search rows that carry no commodity code.

claims.statement: After each search, the service asks MDM once for the commodity records of every distinct code the search rows carry, and leaves out every row whose code MDM flags as germinal (isGerminal true).
The commodity search lists only non-germinal species, so it serves live animals only and offers no search over germinal-product commodities.
claims.quote: "Lists the non-germinal species MDM matches to the term, grouped by code. "

claims.statement: A code MDM does not flag as germinal is listed even when it sits outside the live-animals chapter; a missing isGerminal counts as not germinal.
A species with no Latin name is left out of the search results.
The same species (same Latin name) under the same code is listed once, keeping the first occurrence's common name, even when MDM returns it on both a species row and a commodity row.
claims.note: mechanism: de-duplicates MDM species matches by commodity code and Latin name.

claims.statement: The same species under two different codes is listed under each code, so one species can appear in several groups.
The search lists no more species than the size asked for, in MDM's order, but its total counts every distinct named, non-germinal species match on the MDM page it read.
The search total is the number of species matches on the one MDM page read, not MDM's totalElements, so it does not count matches on later MDM pages.
claims.note: Inferred: totalElements of the MDM search page is never read by CommoditySearchService; the 0102 fixture has totalElements 1 and the endpoint answers total 15. The schema text 'Number of species matching the search term' is therefore true only of the page read. MDM pages are of rows (a commodity row can hold many species), so page and size mean different units to MDM and to this service.

claims.statement: Matching species are grouped by commodity code, with the groups and the species within each group in the order MDM returned them.
claims.quote: Collectors.groupingBy(SpeciesMatch::code, LinkedHashMap::new, ... "Species on this page, grouped by commodity code in MDM's order"

claims.statement: The search response has four required fields: total (number of species matching the term), page (zero-based page number), size (most species the page lists) and groups (species on this page grouped by commodity code).
claims.quote: "Number of species matching the search term" ... long total, ... "Zero-based page number" ... int page, ... "Most species the page lists" ... int size, ... List<CommodityGroup> groups

claims.statement: The search response echoes the page and size the caller asked for.
A commodity group has a required commodity (CN) code, such as 0102, and the list of matching species under that code.
claims.quote: "Commodity (CN) code", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "0102") String code, @Schema(description = "Matching species listed under the code", requiredMode = REQUIRED) List<CommoditySpecies> species

claims.statement: A species in the search has a required Latin (scientific) name, such as Bos taurus, and a common name, such as Cattle or Cow, which is null when MDM holds none.
claims.quote: "Latin (scientific) name", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "Bos taurus") String latinName, @Schema(description = "Common name, when MDM holds one", requiredMode = NOT_REQUIRED, types = {"string", "null"}, example = "Cattle or Cow") @Nullable String commonName

claims.statement: The search response gives each group only its commodity code: it carries no commodity description (such as MDM's "Live bovine animals"), selectability or hierarchy, though MDM returns them.
claims.note: Looked in CommodityGroup, CommoditySearchResponse and MdmProductSearchResult: no description, isSelectable, parentCode or children field is read or returned. A page showing a commodity name beside the code has no source in this service today.

claims.statement: Each GET /commodities call is counted as a commodity-search lookup in the service's lookup metric.
A search logs, at info, how many MDM rows it left out for having no code, how many species for having no Latin name and how many beyond the page size, and logs the germinal codes it left out.
claims.quote: "Commodity search for '{}' leaves out {} MDM rows with no code, {} species with no " + "Latin name and {} species beyond the page size" ... "Commodity search for '{}' leaves out germinal codes {}"

claims.statement: The service exposes a species check at POST /commodities/species-check, which returns the lines whose Latin name MDM does not list under their code.
claims.quote: @Operation(summary = "Check chosen species are still listed under their codes", description = "Returns the lines whose Latin name MDM does not list under their code.") ... @PostMapping("/species-check")

claims.quote: @ApiResponse(responseCode = "200", description = "The lines MDM does not list") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "400", description = "The body is not a list of complete lines") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "503", description = "MDM unavailable")

claims.statement: The species check request has one required field, lines: the commodity lines whose species to check against MDM.
claims.quote: "Commodity lines whose species to check against MDM", requiredMode = REQUIRED) @NotNull @Valid List<CommodityLine> lines

claims.statement: A commodity line is a species chosen under a commodity code, with a required, non-blank commodity (CN) code and a required, non-blank Latin name.
claims.quote: @Schema(description = "A species chosen under a commodity code") ... "Commodity (CN) code", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "0102") @NotBlank String code, ... "Latin (scientific) name of the species", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "Bos taurus") @NotBlank String latinName

claims.statement: The species check response has one required field, unlisted: the lines whose species MDM does not list under their code, in the order they were sent.

claims.statement: ADR 0002 lists countries as the domain managed when it was written, with commodity codes and BCPs/POEs planned to be added to this service first.

- **Commodity codes** — to be added to this service initially

claims.note: The code now serves both planned domains (ports of entry, commodities); the ADR has not been updated. Transporters, document types and certification purposes are not named in it.

claims.statement: Under ADR 0002, a domain is extracted into its own service once its complexity, data volume or operational needs make managing it inside the shared service a burden.
claims.quote: When a domain's complexity, data volume, or operational requirements become significant enough that managing it within this shared service becomes a burden, it will be extracted into its own service at that point.

claims.statement: ADR 0002's consequences: adding a new reference-data domain needs no new service, and domains share deployment, monitoring and MDM connectivity.
claims.quote:
- Simpler initial setup — new reference data domains can be added without bootstrapping a new service
- Reduced operational overhead while domains are small
- Shared infrastructure (deployment, monitoring, MDM connectivity) across domains

claims.statement: ADR 0002's consequences: domain concerns must be kept well separated in the code so a later extraction is straightforward, and extraction is a planned activity.
claims.quote:
- As multiple domains grow, the service may become harder to reason about and deploy independently
- Extraction of a domain into its own service later will require effort and coordination; this should be treated as a planned activity rather than an afterthought
- Care must be taken to keep domain concerns well-separated within the codebase to make future extraction straightforward
